mcqs.question: Which of the following is a living organism?
mcqs.explanation: A tree shows all the characteristics of life – it grows, needs food, respire, and can respond to its environment. Rock, water and plastic do not show any of these characteristics, so they are non‑living.

mcqs.learning_point: Growth as a characteristic of living organisms
mcqs.question: Why is growth considered a sign that something is alive?

options.A: Because it changes size over time due to cell division
options.B: Because it can be painted larger
options.C: Because it can be moved by wind

mcqs.answer: Because it changes size over time due to cell division
mcqs.explanation: Living organisms grow by increasing the number of cells (cell division) or by enlarging existing cells. Painting, wind movement, or light reflection are not biological growth processes, so options B, C and D are incorrect.

mcqs.learning_point: Movement as a characteristic of living organisms
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes movement in living things from movement in non‑living things?

options.A: Living things can move on their own, while non‑living things move only when acted upon by an external force
options.B: Living things never move, but non‑living things always move
options.C: Both living and non‑living things move in exactly the same way
options.D: Only non‑living things can move without any energy

mcqs.answer: Living things can move on their own, while non‑living things move only when acted upon by an external force
mcqs.explanation: Living organisms have internal energy and mechanisms (muscles, flagella, etc.) that allow self‑initiated movement. Non‑living objects move only when an external force (wind, gravity) acts on them. Options B, C and D contradict this definition.

mcqs.question: Which of the following needs food (or nutrition) to survive?
mcqs.explanation: Trees obtain nutrients from soil and sunlight, fulfilling the need for food. Rocks, fire and water do not require nutrition; fire consumes fuel, and water is a substance, not a living entity.

mcqs.question: Which example best illustrates the process of respiration in living organisms?

options.A: A human breathing in oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide
options.B: A plant converting sunlight into sugar
options.D: Iron rusting when exposed to moisture

mcqs.answer: A human breathing in oxygen and exhaling carbon dioxide
mcqs.explanation: Respiration is the exchange of gases – taking in oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide – which occurs in humans and many animals. Photosynthesis (option B) is a different process, while melting ice and rusting are chemical changes unrelated to respiration.

mcqs.question: A plant bends toward a light source during the day. Which characteristic of living things does this demonstrate?
mcqs.explanation: The plant’s bending toward light (phototropism) is a response to an external stimulus, showing the characteristic ‘response to surroundings.’ It is not growth (size increase), movement (self‑propelled locomotion), or excretion (waste removal).

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements corrects the common misconception that only animals reproduce?
mcqs.explanation: Reproduction is a fundamental characteristic of all living organisms. Both plants (through seeds, spores, etc.) and animals (through offspring) reproduce. Options A, B and D are incorrect because they limit reproduction to a single group.

mcqs.question: Which process helps an animal remove waste products from its body?
mcqs.explanation: Sweating is an excretory process that eliminates excess water and salts from the body. Breathing is for gas exchange, eating introduces nutrients, and sleeping is a rest state; none of these remove waste directly. Hence, option B is the correct excretion method.
